jurisdictions.name: Grand Rapids / Kent County
notes: Grand Rapids requires a building permit for a pool or hot tub that can reach 24 inches of water depth or more.
The pool permit page asks for a pool installation plan and a site plan showing the pool location on the lot, uploaded with the application.
A non-owner applicant needs a Residential Builders License issued by the State of Michigan, or written authorization from a license holder.
The city points applicants to its Residential Pool Guide and its zoning rules for placement.

sources.title: Overview on Zoning and Permits for Home Renovation Projects
Residential Building Permits (City of Grand Rapids)

jurisdictions.name: Sterling Heights / Macomb County
jurisdictions.office: Office of Building, City of Sterling Heights
notes: Sterling Heights' pool guide covers pools and hot tubs with side walls over 24 inches. It lists a building permit application, plus electrical and mechanical permits where that work applies.
Pool plans must show the location on the property, with the water's edge at least 6 feet from side and rear lot lines and easements.
The plans must also show overhead wires, the electric meter and service line, barrier or enclosure details, and entrapment protection for a pool with a floor drain.
Inspections listed for an in-ground pool include a building open hole inspection and a final building inspection, with electrical inspections if electric is installed.

sources.title: Pool Permit Packet and Pool & Hot Tub Guide (Sterling Heights)

jurisdictions.name: Detroit / Wayne County
jurisdictions.office: Buildings, Safety Engineering and Environmental Department (BSEED)
notes: BSEED says building permits are applied for in the Accela portal, with scope of work and plans submitted through the ProjectDox portal.
BSEED's FAQ says single-family and duplex residential structures may apply in the office.
The Detroit Property Maintenance Code (Sec. 9-1-109) says pools must be fully enclosed by a fence at least 4 feet high with a self-latching gate.
The same section says pools must be installed consistent with the Michigan Construction Codes and have a working water filtration device.

sources.title: Detroit Property Maintenance Code, Chapter 9 (Sec. 9-1-109 Swimming pools)

jurisdictions.name: Ann Arbor / Washtenaw County
jurisdictions.office: Building, Rental and Inspection Services; Planning and Development Services
notes: Ann Arbor takes building permit applications through its STREAM online portal, which handles applications filed since March 2022.
Electrical, mechanical and plumbing trade permits are also applied for in STREAM and are not released until the related building permit is approved.
The city's accessory building handout lists pools among accessory structures. Zoning compliance permits for such structures must be submitted online in STREAM.
